what: Dev-only choice of ONE new configuration of the live v1 segmenter, "v1-policy2": the zero-candidate fallback (already on), a look policy that places first looks on the tiling grid and confirms unsure critical masks with a look that can fire for v1, value weights that favour the critical classes, and a two-tier human gate. Never a held-out set. Pre-registration stub: the grid, the metrics, the rule, the splits, the commands and the choices below were committed before any run of any configuration in the grid; the rows, the hard-subset rows, the matched-budget rows and the verdict are added after by `python -m evals.policy2 build`, which applies the rule as written (evals.policy2.clauses) and asserts these fields unchanged.
motivation: The cold re-grade of the released v1.1.0 (private-assets/regrade-2026-10-21-released.json) found, for v1 on the held-out sets: on CODEBRIM eval200 an L2 tiling grid finds 0.50 of the defects at 0.10 of the pixels against the agent's 0.49 at 0.14; escalation fires on 5.9 % of looks and verify on 9.4 %, because v1's min_view 0.3 makes L2 the finest level on 4608-px photos, so a mask drafted there gets no verify; v1 sends 9.60 critical boxes per CODEBRIM photo to a person (precision 0.077); critical-class recall is weak (exposed rebar 0.16 on CODEBRIM, 0.02 on synth200). The owner asked for one configuration combining (a) the zero-candidate fallback, (b) a look policy that beats or matches L2 tiling at fewer pixels with escalation that can fire for v1, (c) value weights that favour critical classes, (d) a lower human-review load without losing critical-class recall, every critical finding the agent keeps still going to a person.
segmenter: onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx (v1, the released weights c49416c10087...; the fp16 file beside it, unused with the governor's overrides off), under its own profile onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx (min_view 0.3, absorb off), the zero-candidate fallback on (JobConfig.fallback_l2, its default since 7cddb48), resolved by name and weights in every job
costs: fixed: the job_ops p50 ms per call of results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime/micro.json, the table v1's dev comparison (results/dev/model_choice_dev.json), the fallback's dev run and v1's held-out runs were charged; governor overrides off (evals.harness.run_drishyam), caps and KILL on. A confirm look is a look: it is charged its warp, quality and segment:accurate p50 and 512 x 512 px against the cap like any other.

design.a_fallback: JobConfig.fallback_l2 (on, unchanged): a photo whose overview proposes no candidate gets one whole-photo L2 look.
design.b_look_policy: JobConfig.grid: the first looks are the tiles of the first level's 20 %-overlap 512-px grid (agent._tiles, equal to evals.harness.slice_boxes, the tiling baseline's own tiles) that hold an overview candidate's centre, each candidate counted in the first tile that holds it, the tile's prior its candidates' best: no two first looks re-read one tile, and the survey's seeding and the stop rule decide which tiles are read and in what order. JobConfig.crit_confirm: a mask held under the floor (d) gets one confirm look, cause confirm-critical, action verify: 'shift' runs it at the held look's level with the window recentred on the mask (v1's finest level is no obstacle), 'finer' one level finer, past min_view (for this verify look only). A confirm look never escalates and drafts only the held classes it confirms.
design.c_value_weights: JobConfig.crit_weight: the severity term of a region's expected value (agent.Job._score) is multiplied by this when the region was seen (seeded or looked at) as exposed_rebar or spalling, so a region showing a critical class is read before others and the stop rule needs a higher bar to leave it unread. 2.0 in every eligible configuration: the critical classes count double; not tuned.
design.d_human_gate: JobConfig.crit_floor: a mask that would put a new critical finding before a person (critical by area as a finding measures it, joining no critical finding of its class) but whose class confidence is under the floor is not drafted: with crit_confirm its confirm look decides (its own mask at or above the floor, or one overlapping the held mask at IoU >= 0.5: drafted from the confirm look as a critical finding, held critical by the area the held look measured; otherwise not confirmed); without, or not confirmed, or never run, the mask goes to the work order's not_assessed list as kind needs-a-look (class, confidence, box, action check-by-eye), so the order is never ready while it is there and a person still sees it. JobConfig.merge_critical: a critical mask mostly inside (intersection over the smaller box >= 0.5) a critical finding of its class joins that finding, one decision instead of two. Every critical finding the agent keeps is pending_review for a person; nothing is approved by the agent.

variants.cur: v1 as it is (the 45a2bc5 agent with the fallback merged, every policy2 knob off): the reference, listed first, so every other row is paired with it on the same photos and the same cost table
variants.eligible: the 8 configurations the rule chooses from: grid on (g_) or off (n_) x confirm shift (s) or finer (f) x floor 0.6 or 0.7, each with crit_weight 2.0 and merge_critical on (evals.policy2.ELIGIBLE)
variants.ablations: reported, never chosen: g_s60 with one piece switched off (merge off, weight 1, no confirm look, no floor), and the grid alone (evals.policy2.ABLATIONS)

choices: Stated before any run of the grid. Read before this commit, all on dev only: (1) current v1's CODEBRIM dev100 dump from the fallback's dev run (runs/fallback/real.dump.json.gz in that worktree): its critical boxes are 7.24 per photo, 3.80 once merged as the tiling baseline's boxes are, and 2.07 critical findings; of 724 critical boxes, 187 hit a critical ground-truth box; their mean class probability is 0.668 at the median for exposed rebar that hits and 0.551 for rebar that does not (spalling 0.907 and 0.843). Those medians set the two floors, 0.6 and 0.7, and the merge. (2) L2 tiling on dev100 per ground-truth box against that dump: of 837 boxes it finds 56 v1 misses (29 outside every v1 look at L2 or finer, 27 inside one) and v1 finds 29 it misses; on the critical classes v1 finds 173 of 319 and L2 tiling 164. (3) A probe of tiling at the agent's first level restricted to tiles holding an overview candidate: on dev100 6.46 of 6.82 tiles per photo hold one, found 0.5125 at 0.155 of the pixels against 0.5173 at 0.170 for every tile; on synth_dev 5.05 of 6, 0.695 at 0.421 against 0.715 at 0.500. That is why the grid is in the grid and why the rule does not require beating L2 tiling. (4) The dev splits' label sizes, for the hard subset's cut. No configuration with a policy2 knob on was run on any dev or held-out photo before this commit; the behaviours were tested on synthetic photos and the bundled samples only.

The grid is pre-listed and small: 8 eligible configurations, 4 ablations of one of them and the grid alone; crit_weight 2.0 is a round choice, not tuned; the floors were read off current v1's dev confidences (choice 1). Choosing the best of 8 on dev makes the dev numbers of the chosen one optimistic; the single held-out read is the unbiased check.

Two tiers. 'drafted' boxes are those of the agent's findings (evals.harness preds: per component, from every look in a finding's trail), the tier a person signs off when critical; 'shown' boxes are those plus the needs-a-look masks' components (preds_all), every box a person is shown. Overall recall is scored on what a person is shown (a needs-a-look mask is a reported detection, checked by eye); critical-class recall on the drafted tier only, so moving a critical mask from sign-off to needs-a-look can only lose it, never gain it; critical boxes per photo count the drafted tier (the published critical_per_image, the 9.60 the re-grade read); sign-offs per photo count critical findings. On the clean split every shown box is a false alarm.
critical-class recall: exposed_rebar and spalling ground-truth boxes of any size, pooled (found / total), by the harness's match rule (same class, IoU >= 0.3 or the box holds the GT centre).

The critical-box clause asks for a measurable fall on CODEBRIM dev100 and only no measurable rise on synth_dev: the gate load the re-grade measured is CODEBRIM's (7.24 critical boxes per dev100 photo for v1), synth_dev's is 0.82 per photo. Evidence standard throughout (as results/dev/model_choice_dev.json and zero_candidate_fallback.json): a gain needs its paired CI wholly on the gain side; 'does not fall / does not rise' needs the CI not wholly on the harm side.

The matched-budget comparison with L2 tiling is reported, not part of the rule: the probe (choice 3) shows tiles holding a candidate cover nearly every tile on CODEBRIM, so a policy that reads them all cannot read fewer pixels than the grid, and making it a requirement would make the rule test the saliency prior, not this configuration.

Scope: the knobs are JobConfig fields; if a configuration is adopted it becomes the default of v1's profile only (agent.POLICY2 for onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx); the classical engine and v2a-v2c keep every knob off, and every number published before stays that of the knobs off.
rule: Stated before any run of the grid. Reference: cur at the 30 % cap, listed first (evals.dev_sweep's vs_ref fields: paired 95 % bootstrap CIs over photos, 1000 resamples, seed 0). An eligible configuration PASSES only if ALL of these hold at the 30 % cap (evals.policy2.clauses; a CI that could not be computed fails): (1) recall of what a person is shown does not fall, on synth_dev AND CODEBRIM dev100: the upper bound of the paired CI of its recall ratio to cur (recall_all_vs_ref_ci) is >= 1; (2) critical-class recall of the drafted tier does not fall, on synth_dev AND dev100: crit_recall_vs_ref_ci upper bound >= 1; (3) critical boxes per photo (drafted tier) fall measurably on dev100: the paired CI of the per-photo difference to cur (crit_diff_vs_ref_ci) lies wholly below 0; and do not rise on synth_dev: its lower bound is <= 0; (4) critical findings per photo (sign-offs) do not rise, on synth_dev AND dev100: signoffs_diff_vs_ref_ci lower bound <= 0; (5) clean false alarms do not rise on synth_clean_dev: the paired CI of the difference in shown boxes per photo (all_diff_vs_ref_ci) and of the difference in the share of photos with any shown box (images_with_any_all_vs_ref_ci) each have a lower bound <= 0. Among the configurations that pass, the one that finds the most critical-class ground-truth boxes with its drafted tier, synth_dev and dev100 pooled, is chosen; ties go to fewer pixels (the mean of the two splits' pixels_frac), then fewer critical boxes per photo (the sum of the two splits'), then the grid's order. If none passes, none is adopted: the code stays behind its knobs, off by default, and no held-out set is read for it. If one passes, it becomes v1's default (agent.POLICY2) and is scored ONCE on the held-out sets (if_adopted_held_out); nothing is changed after that read.
reported_not_in_rule: per split and configuration: recall (drafted and shown), IoU-only recall, chance recall, precision, boxes per photo, critical boxes per photo (drafted, and merged as tiling's are), sign-offs, review requests, needs-a-look masks and boxes per photo, critical-class recall (drafted and shown) and per class, pixels, modelled ms per job and its paired ratio to cur, halts, looks per level and per action and cause (escalation and verify rates, confirm looks), the ratios to L2 tiling, L1 tiling and the downscale; the same on each split's hard subset (evals.policy2: a critical-class ground-truth box under 1 % of the photo, or no candidate), with the recall of those small critical boxes; on dev100 at a 10 % cap (about L2 tiling's 0.102 of the pixels) cur and the 8 eligible configurations against L2 tiling, by recall of what a person is shown and pixels; whether cur reproduces v1+fallback's dev rows in results/dev/zero_candidate_fallback.json.

decision: Adopted by the rule as stated: two of the 8 eligible configurations pass every clause, g_s60 (grid on, confirm look at the same level, floor 0.6, critical classes x2, merge on) and g_f60 (the same with the confirm look one level finer); g_s60 finds one more critical-class box with its drafted tier (223 of 395 against 222), so it is chosen and becomes v1's default (agent.POLICY2). The four floor-0.7 configurations lose critical-class recall on CODEBRIM dev100 measurably; the two at floor 0.6 without the grid do not cut critical boxes measurably. What it changes on dev100 at the 30 % cap, against v1 as it was: sign-offs (critical findings) per photo 2.12 to 1.34 (CI of the difference -1.08 to -0.50), critical boxes per photo 7.24 to 6.38 (-1.52 to -0.28), 0.14 needs-a-look entries per photo (0.49 boxes) for a person to check by eye, recall of what a person is shown 0.480 to 0.490 (x1.02, CI 0.99-1.05), drafted critical-class recall 0.532 to 0.523 (x0.98, CI 0.95-1.02: not measurably lower, and not higher), verify looks 7.9 % to 12.2 % of looks (4.5 % are confirm looks, 0.27 per photo), escalations unchanged (6.7 % to 6.5 %), pixels 0.142 to 0.145, modelled ms per job 3379 to 3470. On synth_dev nothing measurable moved (no confirm look fired: v1's critical masks there are confident or absent); on the clean split v1's one box on one photo is gone (0.033 to 0 per photo). What it does not do: it does not raise critical-class recall (pooled over both splits it finds 223 of 395 critical-class boxes against v1's 226), it does not match L2 tiling on dev100 (0.490 against 0.511 at 0.145 against 0.102 of the pixels; at the 10 % cap 0.434, x0.85 of tiling, CI 0.76-0.92, at 0.89 of its pixels; v1 0.430, x0.84), and the grid by itself changed little (grid alone: recall 0.483, pixels 0.137, ms 3181). The reduction in the human gate comes from the floor and the merge; the grid makes the floor's cut of critical boxes measurable (n_s60 and n_f60 do not pass that clause).
